title: Supervising students and giving feedback
blurb: Know the SSSA roles, give clear constructive feedback, record performance well and monitor care given by others and by lay carers.
question: A second-year student nurse is on placement. Her practice supervisor has concerns about her medicines knowledge. Who confirms whether she has achieved the placement proficiencies, and what should the supervisor do now?

teach.body: The NMC Standards for student supervision and assessment (SSSA, 2018) separate supporting a student from assessing them. Every student has a practice supervisor, a practice assessor and an academic assessor. In plain English: supervisors teach and give feedback day to day; the practice assessor decides whether practice proficiencies are achieved, using that feedback; the academic assessor, from the university, works with the practice assessor on whether the student can progress.

head: Role
Who
Main job
rows: Any registered health or social care professional
For nursing students: an RN with equivalent experience for the field
Nominated by the university; a different one for each part
Works with practice assessor on progression

teach.caption: Practice assessors are not simultaneously the practice supervisor and academic assessor for the same student. Limited exceptions exist only for some post-registration programmes.

teach.body: Code 9.1: provide honest, accurate and constructive feedback to colleagues. Code 9.2: gather and reflect on feedback from a variety of sources. Code 9.4: support students' and colleagues' learning to help them develop their professional competence and confidence. Annexe A 4.1.3 asks for unambiguous, constructive feedback on strengths, weaknesses and potential for development.

steps.label: Soon and private
steps.sub: close to the event, away from others

teach.body: Annexe A 4.1.5 asks for unambiguous records of performance. Write factual, specific, dated examples of what the student did, what was expected and what needs to improve, in their practice assessment document. Raise concerns early with the practice assessor so there is time for an action plan; a concern first raised at the final interview leaves the student no chance to improve.

teach.h: Monitoring care by others and lay carers
teach.body: Proficiency P5.7 asks nurses to monitor and evaluate the quality of care delivered by others in the team and by lay carers; P5.9 to challenge and give constructive feedback about care delivered by others and agree learning needs. If you see unsafe care, stop it first (Code standard 16: act without delay), make the person safe, then discuss privately. For family carers, teach, observe their technique, give feedback and record the plan.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Staff Nurse Ama supervises Zara
teach.body: Zara, a second-year student, is warm with patients but twice this week could not explain why she was giving a medicine. Ama talks with her privately the same day: she praises Zara's communication, describes the two specific episodes and their risk, and asks how Zara sees it. They agree Zara will prepare drug information for her patients each morning. Ama records dated examples in the practice assessment document and informs the practice assessor, who meets Zara to set an action plan.

teach.text: The practice supervisor does not sign off proficiencies; the practice assessor does, informed by supervisors' feedback. 'Mentor' and 'sign-off mentor' are the old pre-2018 roles.

items: SSSA: practice supervisor, practice assessor, academic assessor.
Any registered health or social care professional can be a practice supervisor.
The practice assessor confirms practice proficiencies; with the academic assessor they recommend progression.
Feedback: timely, private, specific, balanced, with agreed actions (Code 9.1).
Record dated, specific examples and raise concerns early; stop unsafe care first, then challenge privately.

summary: You can now explain the SSSA roles, give unambiguous constructive feedback, encourage reflection and keep clear records of a student's performance. You can also monitor and challenge care given by colleagues and support lay carers to give care safely.

A.q: Under the NMC SSSA, who confirms that a student nurse has achieved the practice proficiencies for a placement?
options: The practice supervisor who worked most shifts
The ward manager at the end-of-placement review meeting
The practice assessor, using supervisor feedback
The academic assessor, without practice input
A.why: The practice assessor conducts assessments and confirms achievement of practice proficiencies, drawing on feedback from practice supervisors; the academic assessor works with the practice assessor on progression (NMC SSSA).

whyNot.0: Practice supervisors contribute feedback but do not confirm proficiencies.
whyNot.1: The ward manager has no assessment role unless acting as the practice assessor.
whyNot.3: The academic assessor works with the practice assessor rather than deciding without practice input.

A.q: A physiotherapist offers to supervise a student nurse during a respiratory placement. Is this allowed under the SSSA?
options: Yes, any registered health or care professional can
No, supervisors must be NMC registrants
No, physiotherapists can assess students but not supervise
Yes, if the student is in the final year
A.why: Under the SSSA, students can be supervised by any registered health or social care professional, supporting interprofessional learning. Assessment of nursing practice remains with a registered nurse practice assessor.

whyNot.1: The SSSA widened supervision beyond NMC registrants.
whyNot.2: The reverse: for nursing students the practice assessor must be a registered nurse.
whyNot.3: Year of study does not affect who may act as a practice supervisor.

A.q: Which Code clause asks registrants to provide honest, accurate and constructive feedback to colleagues?
options: Code 8.2
Code 9.1
Code 11.3
Code 20.1
A.why: Code 9.1: provide honest, accurate and constructive feedback to colleagues.

whyNot.0: Code 8.2 is about maintaining effective communication with colleagues.
whyNot.2: Code 11.3 is about confirming the outcome of delegated tasks.
whyNot.3: Code 20.1 is about keeping to and upholding the standards and values in the Code.

B.q: For a student on an adult nursing programme, who can be the practice assessor?
options: Any registered health professional on the ward
A healthcare assistant with over five years' experience
The student's personal tutor from the university
An RN with equivalent experience for the field
B.why: For nursing students, the practice assessor must be a registered nurse with appropriate equivalent experience for the student's field of practice (NMC SSSA supporting information).

whyNot.0: Other registered professionals can supervise, but the assessor must be a registered nurse.
whyNot.1: Healthcare assistants are not registered and cannot assess.
whyNot.2: University staff act as academic assessors, not practice assessors.

B.q: Tom, a student, communicates well with patients but has twice recorded observations late. How should his supervisor give feedback?
options: Raise it at the next team meeting so others learn
Privately and soon, naming strengths, the issue and next steps
Wait for the final interview to give all the feedback together
Mention it to the practice assessor without telling Tom
B.why: Constructive feedback is timely, private, specific about the behaviour and its effect, balanced with real strengths and ends with agreed actions (AnnexA.4.1.3; Code 9.1).

whyNot.0: Public feedback is likely to embarrass and is not constructive.
whyNot.2: Waiting removes the chance to improve during the placement.
whyNot.3: The student must hear the feedback directly so he can act on it.

B.q: A student moves from part 1 to part 2 of her programme. What does the SSSA say about her academic assessor?
options: The same academic assessor stays throughout
The practice assessor takes over the academic role
An academic assessor is needed in the final part
A different academic assessor for each part
B.why: All students receive a different nominated academic assessor for each part of the education programme (NMC SSSA supporting information).

whyNot.0: The SSSA requires a different academic assessor for each part.
whyNot.1: Practice assessors are not simultaneously the academic assessor for the same student.
whyNot.2: An academic assessor is nominated for every part, not just the final one.

C.q: At mid-placement, Leo's supervisor is worried that he regularly leaves patients' call bells out of reach and does not report changes. What is the best action?
options: Give him more time and see if he improves by the end
Ask a different supervisor to take over without discussion
Record dated examples and inform the practice assessor now
Tell the university to remove him from the placement
C.why: Unambiguous, dated records of performance (AnnexA.4.1.5) let the practice assessor act early with an action plan, giving Leo a fair chance to improve. Feedback should also be given to Leo directly.

whyNot.0: Waiting leaves patient risk and no structured support to improve.
whyNot.1: Changing supervisor without discussion does not address the concern.
whyNot.3: Removal is not the first response; an action plan with the assessors comes first.

C.q: Imogen sees a colleague start to lift Mr Price up the bed under his arms, although his care plan says to use a slide sheet. What should she do?
options: Report it to the ward manager at the end of the shift
Ask her to stop, move him safely, then talk privately
Stay quiet now and write it in Mr Price's nursing notes
Correct her loudly so other staff learn from it
C.why: Code standard 16: act without delay on risks to safety. Stop the unsafe practice, move the person safely as planned, then give constructive feedback privately and agree any learning needs (P5.9).

whyNot.0: Waiting until the end of the shift leaves Mr Price and staff at risk now.
whyNot.2: Staying silent allows harm; the notes are not the place for a staff concern.
whyNot.3: Public correction is humiliating and less likely to change practice.

C.q: A community nurse visits Mrs Joseph, who is at high risk of pressure ulcers. Her husband repositions her by dragging her up the bed. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Teach slide sheet use, watch him, and record it
Tell him to stop repositioning her between nurse visits
Leave a leaflet and check again at the next visit
Arrange for her to be admitted to a care home
C.why: Nurses monitor and evaluate care by lay carers (P5.7). Dragging causes shear, a cause of pressure damage, so teaching a safer technique, observing it and documenting the plan supports safe care at home (NICE CG179).

whyNot.1: Stopping repositioning increases pressure ulcer risk.
whyNot.2: A leaflet without demonstration and observation may not change technique.
whyNot.3: Admission is disproportionate when teaching can make care at home safe.

reteach.title: Coach and referee
reteach.question: In sport, the coach helps you improve and the referee decides the result. Which SSSA role is which?

blocks.h: Separate the coaching from the judging
blocks.body: Practice supervisors are coaches: they teach, demonstrate and give feedback every shift. The practice assessor is the referee for practice: they decide, using the coaches' reports, whether proficiencies are met. The academic assessor is the league official from the university who agrees, with the practice assessor, whether the student moves up. Keeping these roles separate makes assessment fairer.

blocks.text: Feedback saved up for the final interview is not feedback: it gives the student no chance to improve.

explain.body: Practice supervisor (any registered health or social care professional), practice assessor (for nursing: an RN with equivalent field experience), academic assessor (university; a different one for each part).

test.q: Which SSSA role works with the practice assessor to make recommendations about a student's progression?
options: The practice supervisor
The ward manager
The academic assessor
The student's preceptor
test.why: Practice assessors and academic assessors work together on recommendations for student progression (NMC SSSA).

whyNot.0: Supervisors provide feedback that informs assessment.
whyNot.1: The ward manager is not an SSSA role.
whyNot.3: Preceptors support newly registered staff, not students.

explain.body: Support and teach, give clear explanations (AnnexA.4.1.1), encourage reflection (AnnexA.4.1.4), give feedback and contribute records to the practice assessor.

test.q: A student is upset after a patient she cared for died unexpectedly. What is the best supervisor response?
options: Tell her to focus on her next patient
Invite her to talk through the event and feelings
Suggest she takes the rest of the placement off sick
Ask a chaplain to speak to her instead
test.why: Supervisors encourage reflection (AnnexA.4.1.4) and support wellbeing. Talking through the event and feelings helps the student process it and learn, with further support offered if needed.

whyNot.0: Moving on without support ignores her distress.
whyNot.2: Removing her from placement is not the first response to distress.
whyNot.3: Chaplaincy may help, but the supervisor should first offer support herself.

explain.body: Soon, private, specific about behaviour and effect, balanced with strengths, inviting the person's view, ending with agreed actions and a review date (Code 9.1; AnnexA.4.1.3).

test.q: Which feedback statement is most constructive?
options: 'You need to be better with patients on the ward.'
'Everyone thinks you are doing fine.'
'Your documentation has been poor this week, I'm afraid.'
'Explaining first helped Mr Lee relax. Keep doing that.'
test.why: Constructive feedback is specific about the behaviour and its effect and suggests a clear next step (AnnexA.4.1.3).

whyNot.0: Vague criticism gives no clear behaviour or action.
whyNot.1: Vague praise gives nothing to build on.
whyNot.2: This names a problem but gives no example or next step.

explain.body: Unambiguous, factual, specific and dated entries in the practice assessment document; concerns shared early with the practice assessor (AnnexA.4.1.5).

rows.label: Entry
values: '12/3: left 2 call bells out of reach'

test.q: Which entry in a student's practice assessment document best meets Annexe A 4.1.5?
options: '4 May: SpO2 89% not reported; plan agreed.'
'Needs to try harder.'
'Some of the staff have raised concerns about her.'
'Generally OK, but lacks confidence with the patients.'
test.why: Unambiguous records of performance are specific, factual and dated and show what was agreed (AnnexA.4.1.5).

whyNot.1: This is vague and gives no evidence or direction.
whyNot.2: Unattributed hearsay is not an unambiguous record.
whyNot.3: This is vague and gives no example or plan.
